own_solution.law: Stefan–Boltzmann law: P = εσ4πr²T⁴. Equal emissivities give P2 = P1(r2/r1)²(T2/T1)⁴. A coating of thickness q changes the second sphere's emitting radius to r2 + q.
assumptions: The stated equal, constant emissivity applies to both emitting surfaces.
Absorbed radiation is negligible, as stated.
The specified second-sphere temperature applies to its outer surface after any coating.
The coating thickness is radial and uniform.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T298E and TDB9C replace the specified 4.5 cm thickness with 'thin', violating the review instructions' requirement that variants concerning the same quantity preserve its number and unit.

counterexamples: A 1 mm bracket coating satisfies T298E but not TCB5F; these renderings therefore differ in thickness specification, although their radiated-power answers agree.
notes: All physical classifications, wiring and certified answers check out. For either relevant sentence, thicknesses 2.5, 4.5 and 7.5 cm give 19.44, 26.158464 and 38.1024 kW respectively; 26.1585 kW is correctly rounded. Every disconnected sentence preserves 12.4416 kW. The explicitly named numerical minimal pairs preserve number, unit and wording apart from attachment. Pass 2 explains that the two numeral-free controls are intentional, and their twin descriptions are accurate. Nevertheless, the binding review instructions provide no exception to the common-number-and-unit requirement for such controls, so the pass-1 rendering defect is retained. The invalid verdict concerns that rendering requirement alone; the individual physics problems and numerical claims are correct.
